chapter_theme: The breath by weekday (வாரசரம்): on each day of the week the breath should flow through the left or the right nostril, and the yogi who knows the rule, and turns the breath that runs against it, keeps the body sound and comes to bliss.
structure_note: The rule by day (790 to 792), the sun and moon in the two channels (793), what follows when the breath runs wrong (794, 795), and a closing verse tying breath, mind and the reckoning of days and hours (796).

790.reading: On Friday, Monday and Wednesday the breath runs on the left; on Saturday, Sunday and Tuesday on the right; on Thursday it runs on the left in the waxing fortnight and on the right in the waning.
790.nuance: The days are named by their planets: வெள்ளி Venus, திங்கள் the moon, புதன் Mercury, மந்தன் Saturn, இரவி the sun, செவ்வாய் Mars, and பொன் (gold) for Jupiter. Left and right are taken as the left and right nostril, the channels இடை and பிங்கலை of 793.

791.reading: If on Friday, Monday and Wednesday the breath moves steadily on the left, the bright body has no flaw: so the generous one gladly told us.
791.nuance: வள்ளல் (the generous one) is usually taken as Nandi, Tirumular's teacher. The promise is bodily health, not release.

792.reading: The yogi who knows Tuesday, Thursday, Saturday and Sunday in this way is a lord; for those who know how to turn the breath that does not fit the day to the right, there is bliss.
792.nuance: Thursday is here simply a right-hand day, while 790 splits it by fortnight. ஒவ்வாத வாயு வலத்துப் புரியவிட்டு is read as redirecting a breath that runs on the wrong side; how this is done is not said.

793.reading: Moon and sun, alternating over the two fortnights, rise and fall through ida and pingala; life wells up in the middle between them: understand it, discern it and be clear.
793.nuance: Moon and sun are the traditional names of the left and right channels, and the middle is taken as சுழுமுனை (sushumna), which the verse does not name. உயிருக்கு இரந்து in line 3 is unclear.

794.reading: When the breath that has risen moves from the right side to the left, there is trembling, fear and going away; if the risen breath runs strongly, understand the sign in which it rose.
794.nuance: Line 2 is obscure and has variants (அதிற்கஞ்சி, அதிற்றுஞ்சி) that change it; it may name the bad results of a breath on the wrong side. இராசி is taken as the zodiac sign of the moment, which ties the breath to astrological reckoning.

795.reading: The wise one who joins the breath that will not keep to the middle but runs left and right and does harm, and leads it as it should go so that joy is gained, said there is something before the lamp that ends it.
795.nuance: அந்தணன் is taken as Siva or the teacher. முடிகின்ற தீபத்தின் முன்னுண்டு is obscure: perhaps a light at the crown, reached when the breath enters the middle channel.

796.reading: The thing to be searched out is above the adorned flower; the kinds of breath and their sixteen strengths, and the support that wrestles with the straying mind, become the day and the hour.
796.nuance: Almost every phrase is technical: அணிமலர் may be a lotus of the body, பதினாறு may be sixteen measures of breath, and ஆதாரம் a support centre. The last line seems to say the breath itself is the clock, but the reading is a guess. A variant reads முகுத்தமு.
